{\LARGE\bfseries How accurate LIGHT 1Dv0\_2 is}\par
\vspace{4pt}
{\large The 1-D model on v0\_2's chemistry, version \di{version}, on 30
September 2026, with its energy ladder, its system map and its reaction
rates}\par
\vspace{10pt}

\noindent\fbox{\parbox{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}{%
\setlength{\parskip}{5pt}%
\textbf{Bottom line.} LIGHT 1Dv0\_2 runs v0\_2's chemistry file for
file, and that chemistry reproduces the fitted KrF decays [1, 2] within \wi{sc.train.lo}
to \wi{sc.train.hi}\,\% rms and predicts decays that no fit used [4] within \wi{sc.xu_figs5_7}\,\% rms. At the Tahoma laser [5]
on 1Dv0\_2's own power input the centre cell gives
\pctof[1]{\di{tah.s13.c.x}}\,\% of the measured small-signal gain of
\di{tah.meas}\unit{\%/cm}.

The 1-D layer has no measurement to meet. Its centre cell matches v0\_2's
0-D run to \di{ref.dev.248} at 248\unit{nm} on \di{mesh.lo} to
\di{mesh.hi} cells, and at Tahoma the gap average on \di{tah.cells} cells
gives \pctof{\di{tah.s13.g.x}}\,\%, where v0\_2 under the beam drive gives
\pctof{\wi{tah.g0.x}}\,\%. The cells at the walls are unresolved sheaths,
so a gap average approaches the interior only first order in the cell
size and is quoted with its mesh. The C/B emission ratio of Yu and Setser [3] is matched to \wi{sc.ys_ir300}\,\%. No fit used Tahoma's numbers and no rate was set by a laser
measurement, so the Tahoma scores are predictions.

The chemistry's largest misses are on data that conflict with the fitted sets,
\wi{sc.hakuta_fig2} and \wi{sc.hakuta_fig3}\,\% rms on the C-A decays of
Hakuta et al.\ [6] and \wi{sc.bs_tau_b}\,\% on the KrF(B) lifetime of
Burnham and Searles [7], and the VUV yield of pure krypton at low pump,
\pctof{\wi{pure.vuv.x}}\,\% of Morozov's measurement [8].

{\footnotesize [1] Eden, Waynant, Searles and Burnham, Appl.\ Phys.\
Lett.\ 32, 733 (1978). [2] Gadomski, Xu, Setser and Nelson, Chem.\ Phys.\
Lett.\ 189, 153 (1992). [3] Yu and Setser, J.\ Phys.\ Chem.\ 94, 2934
(1990). [4] Xu, Gadomski and Setser, J.\ Chem.\ Phys.\ 99, 2591 (1993).
[5] Spectra Technology, \emph{Experimental Support for KrF Laser
Modeling}, final report to Los Alamos, 19 July 1989, OSTI 10136715.
[6] Hakuta et al., Jpn.\ J.\ Appl.\ Phys.\ 29, 1194 (1990). [7] Burnham and Searles, J.\ Chem.\ Phys.\ 67, 5967 (1977).
[8] Morozov, Heindl, Kr\"ucken, Ulrich and Wieser, J.\ Appl.\ Phys.\ 103,
103301 (2008).\par}}}
\medskip

LIGHT 1Dv0\_2 runs v0\_2's chemistry in every cell of a gap on
Nathaniel's Fluid1D, which it imports and never edits. Its input is
v0\_2's, a power deposited in the electrons, uniform across a
\di{ref.gap}-cm gap between two grounded walls. Fluid1D moves the charged
species and the electron energy between the cells and into the walls
under the field it solves, and every row of v0\_2's network runs in every
cell. The chemistry is v0\_2's file for file. The \di{chem.nfiles} files
that make it have v0\_2's md5 sums, which the generator checks before it
writes a number, so every score of the chemistry is v0\_2's, taken here
from the v0\_2 overview. What the 1-D layer adds has no measurement to
meet, and its tests are internal. With uniform power the interior must be
v0\_2's 0-D run, and at v0\_2's reference point the centre cell's 248-nm
share is v0\_2's to \di{ref.dev.248} on \di{mesh.lo} to \di{mesh.hi}
cells. At Tahoma on 1Dv0\_2's own power input the centre cell's gain is
v0\_2's to \di{tah.s13.dev}, \x{\di{tah.s13.c.x}} the measured value. The
cells next to the walls are unresolved sheaths. They cut
\di{ref.32.cut}\,\% of the input on \di{mesh.lo} cells and
\di{ref.256.cut}\,\% on \di{mesh.hi}, so a gap average approaches the
interior first order in the cell size. The stage computes every rate as
v0\_2's model does, with one difference above 30\unit{eV}
(Section~\ref{sec:rates}). Table~\ref{tab:score} lists every test.

\section{How the numbers were made}

{\sloppy Every number in this note is written by
\texttt{docs/make\_overview\_1Dv0\_2.py}, and those of the chemistry by
\texttt{docs/make\_overview\_v0\_2.py} and
\texttt{docs/make\_system\_map\_v0\_2.py}, from the models themselves, and a
test fails when those files no longer match them. The 1-D script first
compares the md5 sums of 1Dv0\_2's chemistry, \di{chem.files}, with
v0\_2's and writes nothing if one differs. Fluid1D (\di{fluid1d.src})
needs Python 3.11 or later with numba, so the 1-D numbers come from that
interpreter, on four numba threads. The Tahoma runs take ML's B/C
constants and conditions, as the v0\_2 overview's do, with ML bound to
v0\_2.\par}

1Dv0\_2 has no drive, beam or cavity module, which is LIGHT's rule. So it
cannot be scored under Tahoma's electron beam, and the beam scores in
Table~\ref{tab:score} are v0\_2's in 0-D. 1Dv0\_2 is scored at Tahoma on
its own power input (Section~\ref{sec:tahoma}).

\section{The 1-D layer}

Each step of \Dt{} runs the chemistry for \Dth{}, Fluid1D's
transport for \Dt{} and the chemistry for \Dth{} again,
Fluid1D's source-coupled split. The chemistry stage runs every row of
v0\_2's network in every cell with the electron energy, in substeps that
change no density by more than \di{substep.change}\,\% (at most
\di{substep.max} per stage), and reads the rates at each substep's
starting state. The stage's energy source is the given power, plus the
field's positive work on the electrons, minus v0\_2's elastic loss, which
heats the gas. Each cell's $T_g$ rises at constant volume, as in v0\_2.

Fluid1D brings what v0\_2 does not have. It solves the space-charge field
between grounded walls and drifts and diffuses the electrons, the ions and
the electron energy. The ion mobilities are Fluid1D's own cited table for
\Krp, \Krtp{} and F$^-$ in Kr. The electron mobility and diffusion are a
Maxwellian at the mean energy on 1Dv0\_2's own cross sections, and the gas
temperature the transport reads is held at the fill's. The neutrals do not
move, since 1\unit{\mu s} at 1\unit{atm} spreads them by microns. The mean
electron energy is held between \di{eps.lo} and \di{eps.hi}\unit{eV}, so
$T_e$ between \di{te.lo} and \di{te.hi}\unit{eV}.

\section{The interior is v0\_2's 0-D run}

With uniform power, and walls that take \di{ref.256.walls}\,\% of the
input, the cells away from the walls see what a 0-D volume sees. At v0\_2's
reference point the centre cell sends \di{ref.256.c248}\,\% of its input
out at 248\unit{nm} on \di{mesh.hi} cells, where v0\_2 gives
\di{ref.0d.248}\,\%. Over \di{mesh.lo} to \di{mesh.hi} cells it lies within
\di{ref.dev.248} of v0\_2 at 248\unit{nm} and \di{ref.dev.147} at
147\unit{nm}, and its gas ends within \di{ref.dev.tg} of v0\_2's
\di{ref.0d.tg}\unit{K}. On every mesh each cell more than \di{int.cm}\unit{cm}
from the walls sends out the centre cell's 248-nm share to \di{int.dev}.

A band reaches the 1-D chemistry as it reaches v0\_2's. The centre cell on
\di{set.band.cells} cells, with \Krts{} + F at the top of its band,
\di{band.k}\unit{cm^3s^{-1}}, gives \di{band.c248}\,\% at 248\unit{nm} against v0\_2's
\di{band.0d.248}\,\% with the same band, and \di{band.c147}\,\% at
147\unit{nm} against \di{band.0d.147}\,\%.

\section{The stage's rates}
\label{sec:rates}

The stage computes every rate on arrays, and a compiled kernel does the
same inside the substeps. At \di{rates.cells} random cell states, every
species over \di{rates.decades} decades, $T_g$ from \di{rates.tg.lo} to
\di{rates.tg.hi}\unit{K} and $T_e$ up to \di{rates.te.hi}\unit{eV}, with
the bands at their defaults and with the three unmeasured ones set,
\di{rates.n} rates were compared with v0\_2's own \texttt{Model.\_k}. The
rows that depend on $T_g$ and the densities agree \di{rates.static}. The
rows read from $T_e$ tables agree to $\di{rates.table}$, largest just
above the \di{rates.table.te}-eV floor of v0\_2's \Krtp{} + \el{} power
law, where the table interpolates across the law's kink. The
two-temperature tail agrees to $\di{rates.tail}$, and the kernel matches
the arrays \di{rates.kernel}.

There is one difference. The stage tabulates every $T_e$-dependent row on
v0\_2's nodes, which end at \di{rates.temax}\unit{eV}, and holds it there
above. v0\_2's cross-section tables do the same, but v0\_2 evaluates
\Krtp{} + \el{} recombination (\di{rates.above.row}), Shiu and Biondi's
power law, at any $T_e$. Above \di{rates.temax}\unit{eV} the stage's rate
is therefore higher than v0\_2's, by up to \di{rates.above}\,\% among the
random states and by \di{rates.above.ceiling}\,\% at the
\di{te.hi}-eV ceiling. The drained wall cells sit there, and so does a
cell that fails to break down. The interior passes \di{rates.temax}\unit{eV}
only briefly while a low seed breaks down, when few ions exist to
recombine. At Tahoma from a seed of \di{tah.s13.seed}\unit{cm^{-3}}, where
v0\_2's own $T_e$ peaks at \di{tah.s13.0d.temax}\unit{eV}, the centre cell
still gives v0\_2's gain to \di{tah.s13.dev}. The random states of
1Dv0\_2's own rate test stay below the table's edge, which is why that
test passes.

\section{The wall cells and the mesh}

The walls drain the electrons of the cells next to them, and the given
power then heats few electrons there. The mean-energy ceiling cuts what
they cannot hold, and Fluid1D's split gives them the field's positive
work only and keeps out a phantom negative part. Both shrink as the mesh
refines (Table~\ref{tab:mesh}). The deficit of the gap average below
v0\_2's 0-D share falls by \x{\di{mesh.ratio.lo}} to
\x{\di{mesh.ratio.hi}} with each doubling of the mesh, first order in the
cell size. So a gap average is quoted only with its mesh, and the
interior is the model's answer. The walls themselves take
\di{ref.256.walls}\,\% of the input on \di{mesh.hi} cells. The ledger of
every run closes to \di{ref.closure} of the input, recomputing the gap's
chemical, electron and thermal energy from its state.

The cells beside the wall cell do not converge. The first of them sends
out \di{ref.32.second}, \di{ref.64.second}, \di{ref.128.second} and
\di{ref.256.second}\,\% on \di{set.mesh.1} to \di{set.mesh.4} cells, moving
away from the interior's value as the mesh refines. On \di{mesh.hi} cells
the cells alternate about the interior value, and $n_e$ and $T_e$ with them
(Figure~\ref{fig:gap}), out to \di{ref.256.reach}\unit{\mu m} from the wall
before they agree with the centre cell to \di{near.tol}. The cells there
are \di{cell.um}\unit{\mu m} wide, and the Debye length in the interior at
mid-pulse is \di{debye.um}\unit{\mu m}, so no mesh here resolves the
sheath, and the alternation is the unresolved sheath's, not physics. It
largely cancels in the gap average, which still converges.

\section{The time step}

The split and the stage are first order in \Dt{}. The stage reads the
rates at each substep's start, so a steady state is exact, and the error
lies in transients. In a \di{dt.pulse}-ns pulse on \di{dt.cells} cells the
centre cell's $T_e$ differs from v0\_2's by at most \di{dt.50}\,\% at
\di{set.dt.1}\unit{ps}, \di{dt.25}\,\% at \di{set.dt.2}\unit{ps} and
\di{dt.12.5}\,\% at \di{set.dt.3}\unit{ps}, and each halving of the step
cuts the error by
\x{\di{dt.ratio.lo}} to \x{\di{dt.ratio.hi}}. The reference point runs at
\di{ref.dt}\unit{ps}.

\section{Tahoma and the seed}
\label{sec:tahoma}

At Tahoma's conditions, \di{tah.f2torr}\unit{Torr} of F$_2$ in Kr at
\di{tah.torr}\unit{Torr}, \di{tah.pin}\unit{kW\,cm^{-3}} for
\di{tah.pulse}\unit{ns}, with ML's constants imposed and $g_0$ from KrF(B)
over \di{tah.win.lo} to \di{tah.win.hi}\unit{ns} on \di{tah.cells} cells,
1Dv0\_2's centre cell gives v0\_2's own-input gain to \di{tah.s13.dev}
from a seed of \di{tah.s13.seed}\unit{cm^{-3}} and to \di{tah.s15.dev}
from \di{tah.s15.seed} (Table~\ref{tab:tahoma}). That is
\x{\di{tah.s13.c.x}} the measured \di{tah.meas}\unit{\%/cm}. The gap
average, lowered by the wall cells, is \x{\di{tah.s13.g.x}}. The power
input sets the electron gas apart from the beam's (the v0\_2 overview,
Section~8), so this gain does not test the input either.

From ML's own seed, \di{tah.ml.seed}\unit{cm^{-3}}, 1Dv0\_2 never breaks
down. v0\_2's 0-D $T_e$ runs to \di{tah.ml.0d.temax}\unit{eV} from that
seed before its tail reaches the Kr thresholds, and 1Dv0\_2 holds $T_e$
below \di{tah.te.cap}\unit{eV}, so the ceiling cuts \di{tah.ml.cut}\,\% of
the input and no KrF forms. From \di{tah.s13.seed} v0\_2's 0-D $T_e$ peaks
at \di{tah.s13.0d.temax}\unit{eV}. So 1Dv0\_2 needs a seed of
\di{tah.s13.seed}\unit{cm^{-3}} or more at these powers, while v0\_2's own
gain barely moves with the seed.

\section{The chemistry}

The chemistry is v0\_2's, and the v0\_2 overview gives its accuracy in
full. In short, the KrF(B,C) block is a joint fit to the three kinetic
measurement sets that agree, matched to \wi{sc.train.lo} to
\wi{sc.train.hi}\,\% rms, and it predicts the held-out decays of Xu et
al.\ to \wi{sc.xu_figs5_7}\,\%. The KrF(B) radiative lifetime,
\wm{tauB}\unit{ns}, is the one KrF rate neither measured nor fitted. Under
Tahoma's beam v0\_2 gives $g_0$ at \x{\wi{tah.g0.x}}, $I_\mathrm{sat}$ at
\x{\wi{tah.isat.x}} and \gIP{} at \x{\wi{tah.eta.x}}, and over the B/C
posterior $g_0$ spans \wi{post.g0.lo} to \wi{post.g0.hi}\unit{\%/cm}. The
\Krts{} route is basic, and the rates known only as a published spread are
bands whose default is a measurement or 0. Two bands matter at the
reference point, \Krts{} + F (\wm{bd.kr2_f.lo248} to
\wm{bd.kr2_f.hi248}\,\% at 248\unit{nm}) and the trimer's temperature law
(\wm{bd.trimer_tg_pow.lo248} to \wm{bd.trimer_tg_pow.hi248}\,\%). A band
set in 1Dv0\_2 (\texttt{Params1D.rates}, \texttt{-{}-rate}) is a constant
of the run in every cell, as in v0\_2.

\section{The system map}

In the interior each cell is v0\_2's 0-D run, so its energy flow is v0\_2's
map on the page after the gap figure. Figure~\ref{fig:gap} shows the gap
itself at the reference point. The 248-nm share of each cell's own input
is v0\_2's value away from the wall on every mesh. It drops to nearly
nothing in the wall cell, which narrows as the mesh refines, and on the
finest mesh the cells beside it alternate about the interior value. At
\di{prof.t}\unit{ns}, mid-pulse, the finest mesh shows the wall cell's
electrons drained and held at the mean-energy ceiling, and $n_e$ and $T_e$
alternating beside it.

\section{The energy ladder}

1Dv0\_2 runs v0\_2's network in every cell, so its energy ladder,
Figure~\ref{fig:ladder}, is v0\_2's. It places every species at its
formation energy, the energy above ground-state Kr and \Ft{} at rest that
Appendix~A lists, and draws the rows that move energy between them, as the
ladder view of the website's excimer simulation does. KrF(B) lies \lad{DeB}\unit{eV} below the ion pair \Krp{} + \Fm{}, the
measured $D_e(B)$, and \lad{BoverKrF}\unit{eV} above Kr + F. The
\lad{wl.G4}-nm photon carries \lad{hv.G4}\unit{eV} of that and leaves
KrF(X) only \lad{heat.G4}\unit{eV} above Kr + F. The harpoon G3 heats the
gas by \lad{heat.G3}\unit{eV} for each KrF(B) it makes, the ion-ion
recombination K26 by \lad{heat.K26}\unit{eV} and the trimer's formation by
\lad{heat.G5}\unit{eV}. \KtF{} emits \lad{hv.C3}\unit{eV} at
\lad{wl.C3}\unit{nm} and leaves \lad{heat.C3}\unit{eV} of lower-state
repulsion. On the \Krts{} route, which is basic in v0\_2, \Krts{} emits
\lad{hv.V}\unit{eV} at \lad{wl.V}\unit{nm} and leaves
\lad{heat.V}\unit{eV}, or meets F$_2$ and makes KrF(B) through NK7 or
\KtF{} through K2F\_BR.
The 1-D layer adds no level and no row. It moves the charged species and
the electrons' energy between the cells and into the walls.

\begin{figure}[p]
\centering
\ladpicture
\caption{The energy ladder of LIGHT v0\_2, version \lad{version}, in eV
above ground-state Kr and \Ft{} at rest. A bar is a species at its
formation energy and a dashed bar a pair, the sum of two. An arrow is a
row, labelled with its id. It is solid in the default network and dotted
for a band whose default is 0, \lad{zero}. The rows of the optional group
\lad{groups} are dashed. A photon's arrow drops by its quantum, and the red
squiggle below it is the heat its lower state gives the gas as it falls
apart. A red stub is a quench. The energy a row releases heats the gas,
except a photon's, which leaves, and that of \lad{toe}, which goes to the
electrons. KrF(B) and KrF(C) lie \lad{gapBC}\unit{cm^{-1}} apart and are
drawn as a pair of bars that every B and C row meets. The rows
\lad{notdrawn} move nothing between levels and are not drawn.}
\label{fig:ladder}
\end{figure}

\section{Where 1Dv0\_2 is not yet reliable}

\begin{itemize}
\item Everything that limits v0\_2 limits 1Dv0\_2, above all \Krts{} + F,
which has no measurement, and the trimer's rate above
\wi{tri.klimek.hi}\unit{K} (the v0\_2 overview, Section~10).
\item Nothing measured tests the 1-D layer. No spatially resolved Kr/F$_2$
measurement is among the sources held, and with uniform power the
transport barely touches the interior.
\item The wall cells are unresolved sheaths, and their share of any gap
average is a property of the mesh. The cells beside them alternate about
the interior and do not converge as the mesh refines. Quote the interior,
or a gap average with its mesh.
\item The transport's own inputs are not LIGHT's. The ion mobilities are
Fluid1D's table, the electron transport a Maxwellian at the mean energy,
and the gas temperature it reads is the fill's. With a nonuniform power
profile (\texttt{-{}-profile}) these would matter.
\item \Krtp{} + \el{} above \di{rates.temax}\unit{eV} runs at its
\di{rates.temax}-eV value, where v0\_2 follows the power law
(Section~\ref{sec:rates}).
\item The seed. At hundreds of kW\,cm$^{-3}$ a seed below
\di{tah.s13.seed}\unit{cm^{-3}} does not break down, and the summary warns.
\item First order in \Dt{} and in \Dx{}, and the mean electron
energy held to \di{eps.lo} to \di{eps.hi}\unit{eV}.
\item No discharge. Fluid1D's circuit would be a drive module, which
LIGHT does not carry, and it would need a field-driven EEDF where v0\_2's
tail is set by the given power.
\end{itemize}
